hostRepair.r3f: A version-scoped shared Three DFG_LUT lifecycle adapter was implemented through public compile/dispose hooks. Production tests remove the prior per-close DOM-node growth without changing the sampled rendered pixels. Development React Refresh retention remains separate; no iframe was added for Three, R3F or Theatre.

limitations: CDP JavaScript heap and DOM counters do not measure GPU allocations, texture memory or driver resources.
Twelve cycles are a bounded observation, not proof against every long-duration or future-version leak.
Only desktop Chromium was exercised for these resource measurements; Safari, physical touch devices and low-memory devices were not measured.
Heap values fluctuate with compilation and browser tooling; no universal safe budget is inferred.
Development source was not pinned to a commit. HMR was blocked within each run, and meaningful conclusions rely on within-run trends and explicit retaining paths.
Package retention findings apply to evaluated versions and must be rechecked when dependencies change.

Post-fix verification measures stable counters; no post-fix heap snapshot was retained. The known pre-fix retaining path is preserved as compact source-backed evidence. Long-duration JavaScript heap plateau remains unverified because both R3F and the native CSS control continued small increases through thirty-six cycles.
